title: Symmetry-Reduced Variational Quantum Simulation of the $U(5)\rightarrow SU(3)$ Quantum Phase Transition in the Interacting Boson Model
abstract: The spherical-to-deformed quantum phase transition of the Interacting Boson Model (IBM) is investigated using the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). The $U(5)$--$SU(3)$ transitional Hamiltonian is studied with $χ=-\sqrt{7}/2$. We develop a symmetry-preserving, minimum-qubit VQE framework for collective nuclear models, achieving a substantial reduction in qubit requirements without compromising the finite-size quantum-phase-transition physics. The transition is characterized through the normalized $d$-boson occupation and ground-state energy derivatives. Finite-size results are found to approach the analytic critical point $ξ_c=8/17\simeq0.470588$, with an independent order-parameter extrapolation yielding $ξ_\infty=0.46986(61)$. The VQE reproduces ground-state energies and structural observables to numerical precision. These results demonstrate the potential of symmetry-reduced VQE for efficient quantum simulations of collective nuclear dynamics and quantum phase transitions.
summary: This work uses a symmetry-reduced Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) to study the quantum phase transition in the Interacting Boson Model. By analyzing finite-size scaling of order parameters, the authors demonstrate that the VQE approach can efficiently and accurately simulate this transition, confirming theoretical predictions for the critical point.
main_problem: The paper investigates the quantum phase transition from the spherical $U(5)$ limit to the deformed $SU(3)$ limit within the Interacting Boson Model (IBM).
main_result: The symmetry-reduced Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) successfully simulates the QPT, reproducing structural observables and approaching the analytically predicted critical point $\xi_c = 8/17$.
method: The study employs a symmetry-preserving, minimum-qubit VQE framework combined with finite-size scaling and thermodynamic-limit extrapolation techniques.
model_or_system: The system is the Interacting Boson Model (IBM), which describes the low-lying collective states of even-even nuclei. The Hamiltonian is parameterized by control variables $\xi$ and $\chi$.
key_observables: Normalized d-boson occupation ($\rho_d$) used as the primary order parameter, ground-state energy ($E_0$), and quadrupole collectivity ($	ext{CQ}$).
important_parameters: Control parameters $\xi$ and $\chi$; the critical point $\xi_c = 8/17 \approx 0.470588$.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that symmetry reduction based on rotational invariance is valid for minimizing qubits while preserving the finite-size physics of the QPT.
figures_summary: Figures compare VQE results against exact diagonalization benchmarks, showing convergence of finite-size indicators toward the analytic critical point $\xi_c$.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the IBM Hamiltonian, develops a symmetry-reduced VQE workflow, benchmarks this method against exact diagonalization results, and analyzes the finite-size scaling of order parameters to extrapolate the true thermodynamic critical point.
why_interesting: The application of quantum simulation techniques (VQE) to model a well-established nuclear structure model (IBM) provides a concrete testbed for quantum algorithms in condensed matter/nuclear physics, particularly for studying phase transitions.
